chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muʿammar ibn Khallād, who said:
A man from the people of Persia asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and said to him: “Do you know the unseen?”
So he said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “Knowledge is spread out for us, so we know; and it is withheld from us, so we do not know.”

And he said: “The secret of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, He confided it to Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, and Jibrāʾīl confided it to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله, and Muḥammad confided it to whomever Allah willed.”

key_terms.أَسَرَّهُ: He confided it secretly or entrusted it confidentially
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: knowledge granted and disclosed by Allah
key_terms.الْغَيْبَ: the unseen reality hidden from ordinary human perception
key_terms.سِرُّ: a divine secret or concealed matter
key_terms.يُبْسَطُ: is expanded or spread out, meaning made available

ai.seo_question: Do the Imams know the unseen independently or only by Allah’s permission?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that knowledge of the unseen is not independently possessed, but is granted by Allah when He wills and withheld when He wills. It presents such knowledge as a divinely transmitted secret passed by Allah to Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, then to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله, and then to those whom Allah chooses.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Moammar Bin Khallad who said,
‘A man from the people of Persia asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Are you knowing the knowledge of the unseen?’
So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Knowledge is extended to us<sup>asws</sup>, so we<sup>asws</sup> know it, and it is Withheld from us<sup>asws</sup>, so we<sup>asws</sup> do not know it’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Secrets of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, He<sup>azwj</sup> Confided to JIbraeel<sup>as</sup>, and Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> confided to Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, and Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> confided to the one whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desired’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said that a man from Persia asked abu al-Hassan (a.s.) the following.
“Do you know al-Ghayb (the hidden facts)?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “abu Ja‘far (a.s.) has said, ‘It opens to us then we know it and it is withheld from us then we do not know.”

The Imam (a.s.) then said, “It is the secret of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, who has secretly given to Jibril and Jibril has secretly given to Muhammad (s.a.) and Muhammad (s.a.) has secretly given to whoever Allah wished.”
